key_insight: BrainAid uses lightweight CNNs and explainable AI to classify four brain MRI categories accurately while staying suitable for low-resource deployment.
clinical_relevance: It could support faster, more accessible tumor screening in settings where specialist review or high-end computing is limited.
method: Trains efficient CNN/ViT-based models on public brain MRI scans
Classifies glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and no-tumor cases
Adds XAI to make predictions more interpretable and deploys the system on a Raspberry Pi
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 98% precision, 98% F1 score, and 98% accuracy on a publicly available dataset, with performance described as better than standard baseline models.
watch_item: Results come from a public dataset, so real-world performance, generalizability, and clinical validation in diverse hospital workflows still need confirmation.
paper_title: BrainAid: Efficient Brain Tumor Detection Using Lightweight CNNs and Explainable AI for Resource-Constrained Environments
